registry_info.name: formation_field
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `formation` family (7 registry names, 3 scripts, 2 vocabularies + 1 outlier). One population of 27 bodies standing simultaneously in five bays as a lattice, a shell, a ring, a column and a drift, so the family's five words are side by side instead of chosen between.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The `formation` word and its five values are PRELOADED from reactive_particle_field.gd at runtime and validated in both directions at _ready; do not retype them here or in the script. This artifact does NOT declare formation as an axis — see dna.declines.

formation_field.name: Formation Field
formation_field.description: Five bays on one apron, each holding the same twenty-seven bodies arranged a different way — lattice, shell, ring, column, drift — the five words read out of reactive_particle_field.gd's own const at build time rather than retyped. The population is generated once from a hash of sin(), so every bay and every tile holds the same bodies in the same order, each carrying a fixed hue from its index; only the arrangement changes. In front of each bay stands a six-slot gauge rail whose bars are measured off the very positions the bodies were placed at. `vessel` is the shape of the container the five arrangements are laid in — the force nobody in the family names. `summary` is how much of the population is summarised beside it. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random.
interactions: walk the five bays and find the same twenty-seven bodies in all five
follow one hue — body 7 is the same body in every bay
at nearest, put the lattice rail beside the drift rail: four bars agree, the last one does not
switch vessel to slab and watch the column bay lose its axis
switch vessel to shaft and watch the drift out-tall the column
formation_field.qfep_connection: Order is not a property of a population, it is a claim about the forces on it — and a claim can only be made about what the container has left unclaimed. The five words the family ships are five such claims, and every one of them has only ever been argued inside a near-isotropic box, which is the one container that asserts nothing. Put the same five arrangements in a slab and `column` stops meaning anything, because the box has already flattened everything; put them in a shaft and `column` stops meaning anything for the opposite reason, because the box has already given everything an axis. The dark spot is the second axis: `spread` is the summary a physicist reaches for first, and under it a lattice and a scatter of the same bodies are the same object. The artifact's own answer is one orange bar wide.
formation_field.relationships: Synthesised from the seven registry names that declare `formation` — reactive_particle_field, reactive_particles, edge_particles, emergence_zone (four tokens on one scene), rigid_sculpture, delaunay_triangulation_3d_cell and organic_space. Replaces none of them and re-runs none of their axes from the outside.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The apron is 3.022 m along X by 0.821 m along Z, so a 4 x 1 clear patch. All five gauge rails face +Z and every bay reads from that one side, so this is a one-sided exhibit and `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you aim it. Standing height is 0.774 m at the tallest vessel, which is table height — the visitor looks DOWN into the bays, which is the reading position the whole layout assumes. There is no collider anywhere in the file, so the pathfinder will route straight through the bays; that is correct, because there are no bays, there is a picture of five.

measurements.measured_by: Computed from the script's own layout constants and re-derived in a Python replica of the geometry; no Godot was run, per the brief. THIS IS THE UNION across all nine tiles, which is what the capture camera fits. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every drawn node in this artifact is a MeshInstance3D (BoxMesh for the apron, decks, sockets and bars; SphereMesh for the 135 bodies). No MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG, no particles, no Label3D, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present. X is 3.022 = five bays at 0.600 pitch plus the WIDEST deck (slab, 0.542) plus 0.040 of apron margin each side; the apron is sized for the widest vessel and is therefore identical in all nine frames, which is why X and Z never move. Z runs -0.511 (slab deck back edge) to +0.310 (apron front lip). Y is the only dimension the axes move: 0 to 0.608 at the cube, 0 to 0.437 at the slab, 0 to 0.774 at the shaft (deck top 0.240 + body diameter 0.028 + vessel height 0.506). Y starts at 0 — the apron underside — so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed.

dna.axis_shape: `vessel` sits SIDE BY SIDE — three containers, none contained in another, each asserting a different thing (nothing, a plane, an axis), so they are a set and any two are a comparison. `summary` NESTS — none is contained in spread is contained in nearest, each rung keeping every mark the last one drew IN THE SAME SIX SLOTS and adding to it, so it is a ladder. Declared parallel-first for law 15, and both value lists are written DEFAULT-FIRST because build_dna_gallery trims from the TAIL: a capped run keeps [cube, slab] (the isotropic control against the loudest contrast) and [nearest, none] (the ladder's top rung against its floor, the most informative two-value truncation available). Written in reading order the summary axis would truncate to [none, spread] and throw away the only rung that answers anything. 3 x 3 = 9 variants, under the gallery's default cap of 16, so no trim is expected.
dna.default:
vessel=cube, summary=nearest. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `cube`. It is the only one of the three vessels that asserts nothing. The family's five words are five claims about a force, and in an isotropic container whatever the five arrangements differ by is THEIRS. The slab and the shaft are the interesting frames precisely because the container has taken part of the claim back, and that only reads as a finding if the visitor has met the control first. The cube is also the family's own condition: five of the seven members inherit reactive_particle_field's field_size of (2.0, 1.5, 2.0), and delaunay uses a cell_radius, which is a sphere.

WHY `nearest` AND NOT `none` OR `spread`. `none` is the emptiest rung by definition — five arrangements and no way to check any claim about them, which is exactly the picture the family's members can already produce. `spread` is the trap the artifact exists to spring, and a visitor who meets only that rung leaves believing the lattice bay and the drift bay hold the same thing. `nearest` is the only rung where the whole finding is in ONE frame: the four white bars of those two bays agree to within 3.3 px of a 22.5 px bar, and the orange bar beside them reads 0.0 px against 39.9 px.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the seven `formation` declarations leave unbuilt: every member can be caught in exactly one arrangement, because a population can only stand one way at a time, and not one of them can put two of the five side by side.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NEVER RETYPED. formation_field.gd opens with
const FIELD_SRC := preload("res://commons/interfaces/qfep/reactive_particle_field.gd")
and the five bays, their names, their order and their count all come out of FIELD_SRC.FORMATIONS at build time — the bays ARE the family's array, not a copy of it. The const is read directly as FIELD_SRC.FORMATIONS rather than through Object.get() (which returns null, because a const is not a property, and would have fallen back silently to this file's own list — the exact drift the preload exists to prevent) and rather than through get_script_constant_map() (which does not PARSE on a preloaded class: it is non-static). Reading the const directly has the best failure mode of the three, because if reactive_particle_field ever drops it this file stops parsing and the compile gate says so on the spot. _check_family_list() runs at _ready and push_errors in BOTH directions: a word the family declares that this field has no bay builder for, and a builder this field has that the family has dropped.

reactive_particle_field.gd is the one read because four of the seven registry names are that one scene (reactive_particle_field, reactive_particles, edge_particles, emergence_zone — the corpus's most common hidden family), and because its order is the order five of the six arrangement-vocabulary members declare.

TWO ORDERS, ONE VOCABULARY, AND THE TRIM THRESHOLD. Six of the seven declare the same five words. Five of them declare [lattice, shell, ring, column, drift]; delaunay_triangulation_3d_cell declares [shell, lattice, ring, column, drift] — its own legacy value hoisted to the front, which is a DEFAULT HOIST and not a different vocabulary, and it is confirmed in the code: _formation_points() hands "shell" and every unrecognised word straight back to generate_hierarchical_points(), the untouched shipped generator. The two orders agree on the last three values, so unlike the station kit's `upkeep` family a capped single-axis sweep across this family compares like with like down to --max 3 ({lattice, shell, ring} against {shell, lattice, ring} — same SET, different tile order) and only diverges at --max 2. rigid_sculpture's default is `ring` and reactive_particle_field's is `lattice`, so their DEFAULTS differ while their vocabularies do not, which is the honest signature of a shared word.

THE OUTLIER, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION UNDER THE SAME SPELLING. organic_space declares formation = [chance, erode, accrete, alternate] and its code settles the matter: _op_for(index, coin_bias) returns a CSGShape3D.OPERATION_* constant — UNION or SUBTRACTION — per shape index. Its `formation` is a VERB applied to a solid; the other six are NOUNS naming where bodies stand. The six return positions; the outlier returns a boolean operation. They are not two dialects of one question and no reconciliation was attempted: this field takes the arrangement vocabulary, and organic_space's process vocabulary is left alone, on the record, so nobody reopens it. Its nearest true kin is not here at all — it is a growth/erosion family, and the registry's own `growth` word (crystal_cluster: scatter|druse|lattice|vein) is closer to it than `formation` is.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A FIELD RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

Every one of the seven family members can be caught in exactly one arrangement, because a population can only stand one way at a time. Each member's promotion block describes the five as five answers to 'what does ordered look like'; not one of them can put two answers in one frame. This field stands the SAME twenty-seven bodies five times and varies the container instead.

LAW 2, DECIDED FROM THE MEMBERS' CODE RATHER THAN THEIR PROSE. The five values are SIDE BY SIDE, in all three scripts:

  reactive_particle_field._calculate_grid_positions() opens `match formation:` in which shell, ring, column and drift each fill particle_targets and RETURN, and `_:` falls through to the cubic-grid body below. Five mutually exclusive exits from one switch.

  rigid_sculpture._place_element() is the same shape: one `match formation:` whose every branch assigns ONE position and ONE rotation to the element, `_:` being the shipped ring.

  DelaunayTriangulation3DCell._formation_points() returns one site array and nothing else.

No value contains another and there is no all-at-once reading that is secretly the top rung — the PARALLEL case, which is exactly the condition under which showing them all at once is NOT merely the top value. The field therefore stands all five, exhibits the word, and sweeps something else.

ONE COPY OF THE ARITHMETIC (law 3), READ TWICE. _population() runs once per build and returns 27 points in normalised [-1,1]^3 — which is exactly the box reactive_particle_field scatters its own units in. That one array is handed to all five bays. Within a bay, _seats() computes the world positions the bodies are placed at, and _measure() is handed THAT SAME ARRAY: every bar is measured off the very positions the spheres stand at, so there is no second table of numbers that can fall out of step with the picture.

WHAT IT FOUND, all computed in Python before anything was built. Bar heights in px at the sweep's own framing (221.43 px/m), and the raw statistics in metres:

  cube      sigma_x  sigma_y  sigma_z  sigma_r | meanNN     CV
  lattice    22.5     22.5     22.5     10.3   |  46.0     0.0
  shell      23.9     23.9     23.9      0.1   |  43.7     2.3
  ring       26.4      0.0     26.4      0.0   |  14.4     0.0
  column      6.4     24.8      6.4     10.7   |  12.8     0.0
  drift      22.3     25.8     21.9     12.8   |  28.8    39.9

THREE THINGS IN THAT TABLE ARE THE ARTIFACT.

(1) A LATTICE AND A DRIFT ARE THE SAME POPULATION under the summary the family would reach for first. 22.5/22.5/22.5/10.3 against 22.3/25.8/21.9/12.8 — the four white bars agree to within 3.3 px of a 22.5 px bar, and three of the four to within 0.7. In metres: sigma_x 0.0925 against 0.0914, sigma_z 0.0925 against 0.0897. A second-moment summary cannot see the difference between positions imposed from outside and positions that are merely where things ended up. The CV bar can: 0.0000 against 0.4918, which is an EMPTY SOCKET beside a 39.9 px bar. That is the whole exhibit in two adjacent bays, and it is why `nearest` is the default.

(2) THE CV IS EXACTLY ZERO FOR THREE OF THE FIVE, BY CONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY LUCK. In the lattice, the ring and the helix every body's nearest neighbour is at the same distance as every other body's, so the coefficient of variation of the nearest-neighbour distance is 0 to the last bit. The shell's Fibonacci quasi-lattice is 0.0281 — nearly regular, not quite. The drift is 0.4918. The gauge therefore does not merely rank the five: it partitions them into 'has a rule' and 'has none', and the boundary case is the one the family calls a membrane.

(3) `column` IS THE ONE PLACE THE FAMILY DISAGREES WITH ITSELF, and this field takes the majority ON THE RECORD. rigid_sculpture._place_element() stacks its elements at x = z = 0 up Y under a quarter-turn screw; DelaunayTriangulation3DCell._column_points() is commented 'a narrow shaft up Y, full height, one twelfth of the radius wide'. Two members read `column` as A SHAFT. reactive_particle_field._targets_column() instead lays five stacked plates of twenty at 0.72 of the box, which is STRATA — and strata at 27 bodies ARE a lattice: a 3 x 3 x 3 grid is three stacked plates of nine, so that reading would have made two of the five bays the same picture. The shaft wins. The degeneracy in the strata reading is a finding about the vocabulary and is recorded here rather than hidden: at this count, one member's `column` and the family's `lattice` are the same arrangement.

THE HELIX RADIUS IS FIXED BY THE BODIES, NOT BY TASTE, and delaunay's proportion was tried and rejected with numbers. At delaunay's cell_radius/12 = 0.0833 of the half-width, consecutive bodies on this helix stand 0.0170 m apart in the cube, 0.0167 in the slab and 0.0214 in the shaft, against a body DIAMETER of 0.0280 — every one interpenetrating. 0.12 and 0.18 also touch. 0.22 is the smallest value tried at which nothing overlaps in any vessel: the step is sqrt(chord^2 + dy^2) = sqrt(0.02862^2 + 0.01308^2) = 0.0315 m in the cube. Delaunay's proportion is honest for its own artifact, whose sites are 0.08 m spheres in a much larger ball; it is not transferable, and saying so is cheaper than a sweep that photographs a smear.

THE VESSELS ARE EQUAL IN VOLUME AND NOT IN EXTENT: 0.039304, 0.039263 and 0.039388 cubic metres, a spread of 0.318%. The three containers differ in SHAPE and not in how much room they give, so a bay that looks emptier is not a bay with fewer bodies in it — which is the confound a naive slab/shaft would have introduced, and it was designed out before anything was built.

THE COUNT IS 27 AND NOT 100 FOR TWO REASONS, ONE PEDAGOGICAL AND ONE MECHANICAL. It is a perfect cube, so `lattice` is a complete symmetric 3 x 3 x 3 rather than the family's truncated fill (reactive_particle_field asks for 100 and lays a 5 x 5 x 5 grid, filling 100 of 125 slots, so its lattice is four fifths of a cube with a bite out of one corner). And it is what keeps the bodies apart: at 27 the tightest gap anywhere in the fifteen bays is 0.0292 m against a 0.0280 m diameter — the ring in the shaft — and that single number is the binding constraint on the entire layout.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own corner background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5%. The numbers below come from ray-tracing this exact geometry at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.56) in Python against the sweep's own _stage_default rig — background (0.055, 0.055, 0.070), ambient (0.62, 0.65, 0.72) at 0.55, a key DirectionalLight3D at 1.25 rotated (-42, -35, 0) and a fill at 0.45 rotated (-20, 130, 0), filmic tonemap — then pushing the result through that same pipeline.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS summary `nearest` <-> `spread` AT THE SLAB, PREDICTED 8.13% FOCUS (0.41% frame). It is a cluster of three, not a single pair: slab 8.13%, shaft 8.29%, cube 8.31%. The fourth thinnest pair in the whole sweep is `none` <-> `spread` at the cube, at 23.15% — nearly three times the gap. The clustering is part of the claim: nearest -> spread adds exactly the same two sockets and two bars per bay at every vessel, so the three numbers should sit within about a quarter of a point of each other. If they spread by more than a point, the sweep is not holding the vessel fixed across the summary rung.

THE ARITHMETIC, because a rasteriser is not an argument. At 221.43 px/m an orange bar is 15.94 px wide. Their heights across the slab's five bays are meanNN 22.9 / 42.8 / 20.4 / 16.7 / 29.4 px and CV 0 / 11.0 / 0 / 0 / 23.9 px, summing to 167.1 px of height, so the added bars carry 15.94 x 167.1 = 2663 px^2, and the ten extra sockets (18.16 x 2.2 px) add about 400 px^2 — 3063 px^2 in total. The union crop at the slab is 645 x 240 = 154,800 px, so 1.98% of the crop changes. The critic's hottest-5% window is 1280 of 25,600 samples, which is 2.5x the changed set, so at most 40% of the window can be non-zero; a bar reads about 150 grey against the apron's 55, which is 95/255 = 37%. The ceiling is therefore 0.40 x 0.37 = 14.8% and the rasterised value is 8.13%, the shortfall being the 4.03x box downsample blending every bar edge into its background.

AXIS MEANS over the 9 same-axis pairs each: vessel focus 63.95% (min 54.21 cube|shaft at summary=none, max 71.69 slab|shaft at summary=spread); summary focus 18.92% (min 8.13, max 25.33). Both should read BITES.

IT SHOULD NOT BE FLAGGED AS A TWIN, AND THAT IS A CLOSE CALL WORTH RECORDING. 8.13% clears the critic's 6.0% TWIN_FOCUS bar by 2.1 points and its 3.0% INERT_FOCUS bar by 5.1, but it sits under the 12.0% WEAK_FOCUS bar, so the pair itself is a weak pair inside an axis whose mean is not. If it comes back under 6.0% the likeliest cause is not the design: it is that the gauge rail was rendered at the FIRST cut's dimensions (0.034 m bar on a 0.054 m slot), which the same rasteriser measured at 4.99-6.17% — see dna.framing_why for why that geometry failed law 4 independently.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks like it should be. `cube` <-> `shaft` is the thinnest vessel pair at 54.21%, and the naive expectation is that cube and slab should be the close ones, since both are wide. They are not: cube|slab is 65.06% and slab|shaft is 71.26%. The reason is that the union AABB is fixed by the apron, so the camera never moves, and a vessel change moves every one of the 135 bodies AND rewrites all thirty bars. If any vessel pair comes back under about 30% the bodies are not moving — check that `vessel` is reaching the artifact at all.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS.
(a) If ANY pair reads 0.00%, run tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=formation_field first: a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles.
(b) If the summary pairs come back materially ABOVE this prediction, the likeliest cause is shadows: the replica has no shadow map, and the key light here has shadow_enabled, so ten added bars each cast a small shadow onto the apron that this prediction does not count. That would make the prediction low, not the artifact wrong.
(c) If the subject share comes back under about 6%, the framing was not read from the registry — this artifact needs 0.56 and at 1.0 it renders a 3 m hall inside a 6.13 m frame.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL NINE FRAMES, not from the default. Union 3.0220 x 0.7740 x 0.8210; diagonal sqrt(9.1325 + 0.5991 + 0.6740) = 3.2258, radius 1.6129. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 puts the camera at 1.6129 / 0.305731 x 1.9 = 10.0234 m and shows a 6.1290 m frame around a 3.02 m object. THIS IS THE FIT-BY-DIAGONAL FAULT ON A WIDE FLAT SUBJECT: the box is 3.9x wider than it is tall, so its diagonal is essentially its width, and PAD then shows 1.9x that again.

AT 0.56 the camera comes to 5.6131 m and the frame to 3.4322 m, which is 221.43 px per metre. Rasterised at that setting the subject's bounding box spans 84.9% of frame width and 31.6-38.0% of height, with 28 px of clear margin on the tight side (the right, because the camera yaws 0.62 and the +x end of the apron comes toward it), and the subject covers 12.1-13.0% of the frame depending on the variant. 0.55 was measured too (86.4% of width, 221 px/m, 21 px on the tight side) and rejected: 21 px is thinner than a replica with no shadow map and an analytic sphere should be trusted to within, since Godot's 12-segment SphereMesh is inscribed in the analytic ball and its shadows fall outside it. 0.50 CLIPS — the apron runs off the right edge.

LAW 10 CHECK, BECAUSE 12.5% SUBJECT LOOKS LOW. It is not a small subject, it is a SPARSE one, and the box is full in width: 84.9% of frame width against 34% of height. A field of five bays is mostly apron and air between bodies 6.2 px across. taxonomy_hall reports 10.4% for the same reason and is correctly framed; the test is whether the union box is full or airy, and this one is airy by design, because the space between twenty-seven bodies is the thing being compared.

GAUGE CHECK AT 221.43 px/m (law 4), AND IT CHANGED THE ARTIFACT. The critic downsamples its crop 4.03x (645 px of subject box to 160), so a mark must clear about 16 screen px to survive as four samples.
  MARKS THAT ENTER A PAIR DIFF, and must clear the bench:
    body sphere      0.0280 m diameter ->  6.20 px          (vessel moves all 135 of these)
    gauge bar        0.0720 m wide     -> 15.94 px, 0.1-48.7 px tall
    socket           0.0820 m wide     -> 18.16 px, 2.2 px tall
    bay deck         0.400-0.542 m     -> 88.6-120.0 px wide, 46.5 px tall (vessel changes this)
  CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF BOTH AXES:
    apron            3.022 x 0.821 m   -> 669 x 182 px
  THE FIRST CUT OF THE RAIL FAILED THIS CHECK and was rebuilt: 0.034 m on a 0.054 m slot is 7.53 px wide, under two samples after the downsample and at the edge of legibility for a visitor at 760 px. It is now 0.072 m on a 0.084 m slot. Six slots span 0.504 m, clearing the 0.600 m bay pitch by 0.096 and standing at x 1.432 inside the apron's 1.511. The same rasteriser measures the consequence: the summary axis goes from 13.43% mean / 4.99% floor to 18.92% mean / 8.13% floor. That is a consequence and not the reason — nothing about what the bars MEAN changed, only the width of the mark, and 7.53 px was failing law 4 on its own.

THE BODY IS 6.20 px AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. A body is not a mark that has to survive alone; twenty-seven of them in a bay are one silhouette, and the silhouette is what the vessel axis moves. Enlarging the bodies would have forced the vessels apart to keep them from interpenetrating (the binding constraint is already 0.0292 m of clearance at the ring in the shaft against a 0.0280 m diameter) and every bay would have grown with them.
dna.z_stack:
READ FRONT TO BACK FROM THE CAPTURE CAMERA, because a frame is four rails and not a slab — operations_gallery's bezel was one 24 mm plate enclosing the panel face AND every mark its axis drew, and four values photographed as one blank slab at 0.09% with the subject at 70.3% of frame.

  z = +0.310 .. +0.275   apron, front lip. Nothing stands here.
  z = +0.275 .. +0.225   THE GAUGE RAIL: sockets and bars, 0.050 deep. Nothing is in
                         front of these, ever, at any vessel.
  z = +0.071 .. -0.471   the bay decks (widest is the slab; the cube's is +0.000 ..
                         -0.400), top face at y 0.240.
  z = -0.200 +/- half.z  the population, standing IN the vessel above that deck.

NOTHING OCCLUDES A BODY, AND IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN CLAIMED. Each of the three vessels was rasterised twice, once with the bodies alone against the background and once complete. Of the 3914 (cube) / 3661 (slab) / 3888 (shaft) pixels a body owns in the bare frame, the apron, the five decks and the full six-bar rail change ZERO in all three.

THE TWO NUMBERS THAT MAKE THAT TRUE are the deck height and the rail distance, and both are tight. The tallest possible bar tops out at y 0.260 standing at z 0.250; screen-up at this camera is 0.9664*y - 0.1494*x - 0.2092*z, so that bar top sits at 0.2241 minus its x term, while the LOWEST body in the widest vessel — the slab's front edge, y 0.254, z +0.041 — sits at 0.2369 minus its own. Pulling the rail in to z 0.130 breaks the slab; dropping the deck to 0.150 breaks all three.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no RandomNumberGenerator, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children and its own ancestors' metadata. _ready is ungated: it reads config metadata, validates the family list and builds the whole field standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THE POPULATION IS A PURE FUNCTION OF ITS INDEX. _hash01(n) is sin(n * 12.9898 + 78.233) * 43758.5453 minus its floor — the corpus's own hash, character for character from combine_sphere.gd and math_objects_gallery.gd. There is no generator in the file at all, so there is no seed to pin and no stream to get out of order. rigid_sculpture's per-index reseed of a RandomNumberGenerator is the FAMILY's determinism idiom and would have been the closer borrow; it was passed over because its PCG32 stream cannot be reproduced outside Godot, and reproducing this population in Python is what made dna.predicted_degeneracy possible at all. A hash of sin() agrees between GDScript and Python to the last bit, because both evaluate it in doubles.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_vessel / config_summary metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks up to four ancestors for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three validate against _is_vessel / _is_summary, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once — the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value rather than blanking the field.

BOTH AXES ARE @export_enum STRING ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here. Both hints are on ONE line each, so the declaration gate's line parser can see them.

THE .tscn ROOT CARRIES THE SCRIPT. formation_field.tscn is a single Node3D named FormationField with script = ExtResource("1") on the root, so GridInteractablesComponent's apply_grid_config call on the ROOT reaches the logic — the line_interface fault, where the axis was declared but unreachable from any map token.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF BOTH AXES, by construction: the apron. It is sized for the WIDEST vessel and never changes, so the hall is the control and the vessel is the variable — a slab tile is not a bigger photograph. That is also why the union AABB's X and Z never move between tiles and the camera never retreats.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `summary`: all 135 bodies and all five decks. The whole summary axis lives on the rail at the front of the apron. `vessel` should be the larger of the two numbers and is predicted at 63.95% against 18.92%.

THREE READINGS ARE EXACTLY ZERO AND ARE DRAWN AS EMPTY SOCKETS, not as missing slots: the ring's sigma_y and sigma_r, and the CV of the lattice, the ring and the column. The shell's sigma_r in the cube is 0.0004 m, a bar of 0.1 px, and is also drawn as an empty socket. This is deliberate under law 6: a zero here is a TRUE statement about the arrangement (a flat ring has no vertical spread; a helix's every body has its neighbour at the same distance) and the socket keeps the slot visible so a zero can be told from an absence.

NO TEXT ANYWHERE. There is no Label3D and no rendered word in this artifact, so LabelFramer has nothing to bolt a panel behind and no tile contains a caption naming an axis value. The five bays are told apart by their arrangement and by nothing else, which is the point.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check three things before the design.
(1) Was dna.framing read? At 1.0 the camera stands 10.02 m off and shows a 6.13 m frame around a 3.02 m hall; every mark halves.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 3.02 m field is under the 6 m staging cut-off, so it MAY be plinthed, and if it is, the pair AABB grows and every mark shrinks. This artifact wants the default profile.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? This is a PLAN-ISH artifact — five bays in a row, read from 15 degrees above the ground. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it; a probe from directly overhead should separate the vessel values LESS than the canonical camera does (the shaft and the cube have the same footprint from above) and should separate them MORE from a low front elevation.
declines: `formation` AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS. Refused, and the refusal is the design. Decided from the members' CODE, not their prose: reactive_particle_field._calculate_grid_positions() is one `match` with four early RETURNs and a fallthrough, rigid_sculpture._place_element() is one `match` assigning one position per element, and DelaunayTriangulation3DCell._formation_points() returns one site array. Five mutually exclusive exits, no value containing another — the PARALLEL case, which is exactly the condition under which showing them all at once is NOT merely the top value. An axis on the word would demolish four fifths of the exhibit at every turn, and the large number it produced would be a measurement of the field being taken down. The field stands all five, names the word in the registry, and reads the word out of the family's own const rather than retyping it.

AN `arrangement` OR `order` AXIS UNDER ANOTHER NAME. Cut in one line: it is `formation` with the serial numbers filed off, and taking a word's answers without its word is the same dishonesty as taking a word without its answers (folding_past's ruling, inverted).

`count` — 8 / 27 / 64 / 125 bodies. A real question (a lattice of 8 and a lattice of 125 make different claims about how much of the box the rule reaches) and it was cut because it breaks the artifact's own control: the whole exhibit rests on the five bays holding THE SAME POPULATION, so an axis that changes the population makes every cross-bay comparison in every tile mean something different. It also collides with the layout, since 64 bodies at this vessel size interpenetrate everywhere.

ANY ANIMATION, RATE, RELAXATION OR SETTLING. A field of bodies has obvious time-domain axes — how fast the swarm falls into its attractor, how much it overshoots, how long it takes to settle — and the family's own members are literally damped physics fields photographed 1.1 s after birth. Every one of those is invisible to a still PNG. info_board shipped five duration exports and produced six identical tiles. Nothing in this file moves; the arrangements are computed closed-form and placed once.

A FRAME-RELATIVE GAUGE. Every bar is 1:1 in metres against a ceiling fixed across the whole sweep: a white bar of height h means sigma = 0.200 * h / 0.220 m, an orange meanNN bar means 0.120 * h / 0.220 m, and the CV bar means 0.60 * h / 0.220, in all nine frames. Normalising per vessel was considered and rejected in one line: it would have hidden the one thing the vessel axis exists to show, which is that a slab's spread genuinely IS wider than a cube's (sigma_x 0.1312 against 0.0925 for the same lattice). sorting_hall normalised each frame to its own busiest row and its gauge then said nothing about the quantity it existed to show.

A PROXY FOR ORDER. The last bar is the coefficient of variation of the nearest-neighbour distance and nothing else — the plain definition, computed from the same positions the bodies are drawn at. It reports exactly 0.0000 for three of the five arrangements, and that zero is a TRUE statement (every body's neighbour at the same distance) rather than a proxy silently reporting nothing, which is the fault law 6 names. The alternative considered was the raw standard deviation of neighbour distances; it was rejected because an absolute spread shrinks with the container and would have reported a flat vessel as more ordered than a cube.

PADDING THE CLOSEST PAIR. summary `nearest` <-> `spread` is predicted at 8.13-8.31% focus, which clears the critic's 6.0% twin bar but sits under its 12.0% weak bar, and it was left there. It is thin because adding two bars to a six-slot rail on a field already holding 135 bodies is a small addition — 1.98% of the crop. What WAS done is not padding but LAW 4: the rail was rebuilt from a 7.53 px bar to a 15.94 px bar because 7.53 px is under two samples after the critic's 4.03x downsample and marginal for a visitor at 760 px. Making the orange bars taller than the white ones, or giving them their own raised plinth, was considered and refused: it would have made the answer louder than the question, which is field_room's ruling — the more faithful model was the weaker axis, and it was kept.
